questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to grow vegetables in a small garden
Why fewer and fewer young women are choosing to become farmers
Ideas helping female farmers get fairer treatment and prices
The most popular vegetables in the world
questions.why: Neil says they'll look at ideas helping female farmers in Bangladesh and Peru earn a fair price.

questions.q: According to the UN, what share of the world's farmers are women?
options: Over 40%
About 10%
Around 25%
More than 70%
questions.why: Beth says over 40% of farmers globally are women.

questions.q: What problems do female farmers in Bangladesh face at the market?
options: The market is too far away
They aren't allowed to grow vegetables
Their vegetables are often stolen
They are harassed or paid too little
questions.why: Neil says they face harassment or are underpaid for their produce.

questions.q: How does the “Farm to Go” app help women like Poppy?
options: It teaches them to grow new crops
They can sell without revealing who they are
It gives them free seeds
It sends their husbands to the market to sell for them
questions.why: Farmers can sell their produce without revealing their identity and get a fairer price.

questions.q: Apart from more profit, what other benefit does Poppy mention?
options: She can travel to other cities
It saves time for her family and garden
She has made lots of new friends through the app
She no longer has to grow okra
questions.why: She says it saves time, so she can spend time with family and work in the garden.

questions.q: Why does reporter Salman Saeed say the extra three cents “might sound small”?
options: To argue that the app is not worth using
To complain about low vegetable prices
To show that most farmers dislike the app
To show that small gains add up over time
questions.why: He says over the year, average monthly revenue for farmers on the app has risen dramatically.

questions.q: What problem continues in many other places, according to Beth?
options: Men in the family often control the money
There are not enough vegetables
Women refuse to use new technology like apps
Markets are closed to all farmers
questions.why: She says problems continue because the man in the family often controls the finances.

questions.q: How does the project in Peru help female coffee growers?
options: It buys all their coffee beans at a much higher price
It gives them free machines
Members save together so farmers can borrow money
It sends them to study in the city
questions.why: People chip in small amounts, which a farmer can access as a loan, for example for a machine.
